drafted_from: tool:create-a-space's own row (its words, input schema, sample run and steps) and what its sample run answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Start a shared space with this person as its owner and first member, for the caller to store", with {"space":"sample-hike","subject":"owner@example.com","title":"Sample hike","label":"group","records":[]}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and answers the rows to keep, and keeps no row itself.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Start a shared space with this person as its owner and first member, for the caller to store", and give it space (the new space's id, the last part of its record:space row id); subject (this person, the way they are named); title (what the space is); label (group, project, event, one-to-one or stay; group when left out); join (the join rows, as in tool:join-a-space; left out, the space is joined by invitation only); records (the records the ask reads: none for a new space).
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:create-a-space and its input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: the answer says created and the owner's state; its keep lists the record:space row and the owner's record:space-member row, which the caller stores.
